conclusions: The source-visible gap is that the original scheduled Alice click can begin on a pre-schedule chat preview although the canonical task and finite peer journal have completed. The current driver does not use its existing per-element content prerequisite at this call.

The narrow candidate is to pass the already supported fourth click argument at this one call, using the common literal TEST scheduled followed by one space. This accepts the fixture's legitimate reply and complete preview forms. It keeps the existing post-click exact TEST scheduled reply visibility assertion.

This candidate is supported as a harness readiness improvement, not a proved account of the unavailable Claude final movement. It must retain the final point equality and fail if the row moves again; no retry, coordinate substitution, timeout change, extra timer or production UI change is justified.

The two actual successful lanes show that the current click operation can begin before the scheduled preview is hydrated: OpenCode dispatched on the older preview, while Codex adopted the newer preview during stabilization. They do not prove that waiting for the prefix would have prevented the particular Claude movement or that every future lane will pass.

If precise causality remains needed, retain the already compared stable/final point arrays and closed original action identity through the existing error-summary path. No additional DOM/Host/process sample is needed to expose those existing values; such diagnostics are not selected by this advisory.
